extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, peer reviewers, and those interested in research integrity and retractions
extracted.subtask_description: A curated news/reading roundup collecting headlines and links about peer review, retractions, research integrity, and related debates in academic publishing. The page points readers to pieces on peer review best practices, retraction cases, investigation reports, and policy discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction reason: publication was incomplete, inaccurate and misleading
rubrics_metrics.description: "This retraction is in acknowledgement of the fact that the publication was incomplete, inaccurate and misleading due to misapprehension of the facts as established during the parliamentary hearings on the transaction."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This quoted language is presented as an explicit stated ground for a retraction (inaccuracy, incompleteness, misleading content arising from misapprehension of facts). The page does not give further procedural detail but uses the quote as an example of a formal retraction rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Dos and Don'ts of Peer Reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Title referenced on the roundup: "The Dos and Don’ts of Peer Reviewing."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the existence of an item that enumerates best practices and anti-patterns for peer reviewers. The roundup only links the piece (title shown); it does not reproduce the specific dos/don'ts on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make peer review fairer, better and easier
rubrics_metrics.description: Title referenced: "Three ways to make peer review fairer, better and easier."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Points to recommendations for improving peer review accessibility, fairness and efficiency. The roundup lists the article but does not include the three specific ways on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of generative AI in peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Title referenced: "Can generative AI add anything to academic peer review?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flags that the role of AI in peer review is under discussion; the roundup links to a piece considering potential contributions and limitations of generative AI rather than giving concrete evaluation criteria itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve academic integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: "Science will suffer if we fail to preserve academic integrity."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as an overarching normative criterion: maintaining academic integrity is presented as essential to the health of science. The roundup cites this position but does not detail specific policies or enforcement mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due process for research misconduct and whistleblower protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Referenced items: "An Overdue Due Process for Research Misconduct." and "Harvard Should Protect Whistleblowers."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames two related evaluative standards: (1) ensure fair due process when handling misconduct allegations and (2) protect whistleblowers. The page signals these as important principles but contains no procedural specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software citation is maturing alongside data citation
rubrics_metrics.description: "While data citation is increasingly well-established, software citation is rapidly maturing."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicates a quality criterion for reproducibility and credit: software used in research should be cited. The roundup highlights this developing norm but does not provide a detailed citation standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journals that ban replications: criterion of being a serious scholarly outlet
rubrics_metrics.description: Title referenced: "Journals That Ban Replications–Are They Serious Scholarly Outlets At All"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggests an evaluative standard that allowing replication studies is a marker of a legitimate scholarly journal. The roundup references the critique but does not elaborate policy specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of investigative 'sleuths' in enabling retractions
rubrics_metrics.description: "If you take the sleuths out of the equation, it's very difficult to see how most of these retractions would have happened."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asserts that independent investigative efforts (research integrity sleuths) are often crucial to discovering problems that lead to retractions. The page presents this as an observation about how retractions occur rather than an actionable rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crafting investigation reports (NSF OIG insights)
rubrics_metrics.description: Title referenced: "Where's the Proof? NSF OIG Provides Insights on Crafting That All-Important Investigation Report."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Points to guidance on how to structure investigation reports for research-misconduct inquiries. The roundup lists the resource but does not summarize the NSF OIG recommendations on this page.
